claim: The mantra is Sanskrit and invokes lords of the spirits (bhutesvari)
evidence: No source checked; mantra ends 'bhutesvari svaha', consistent with the claim, but not verified.

claim: Grammatical note on Sanskrit root (suffix mya-ga on sam)
'In the language of India' literally means China, often used for Sanskrit
evidence: rgya gar means India and rgya nag means China; the colophon phrase rgya gar skad du is 'in the language of India' (Sanskrit), so 'literally: China' is incorrect.
correction: rgya gar = India (not China); rgya nag = China.

claim: gsol ba dang bzhi'i las = jnapti-caturtha-karman
evidence: Search/wisdomlib summary: jñapticaturtha-karma corresponds to Tibetan gsol ba dang bzhi'i las (Pali ñatti-catuttha-kamma), the motion plus three questions procedure.

claim: 'father and son' refers to Milarepa and his primary heart-disciple (Rechungpa)
evidence: Rechungpa is described as Milarepa's foremost heart son; identification is plausible in context though the passage does not name them.

claim: mi dmigs pa stong pa nyid = anupalambha-sunyata
evidence: Anupalambhasunyata, emptiness of non-perception, in Tibetan mi dmigs pa stong pa nyid, one of the 16/18 emptinesses.

claim: Text is a phonetic rendering of Sanskrit ritual formula naming Lokanatha and Ishvara
Description of diagrams
ltung byed = payantika
evidence: Patayantika/payantika (offense of downfall, 'causing fall') is rendered in Tibetan as ltung byed.

claim: Leaf continues Sanskrit praise of Tara in transliteration
Vinaya legal distinction on time-based vs mental concealment
Venuvana is a famous monastery near Rajgir (Bamboo Grove)
evidence: Venuvan, the Bamboo Grove near Rajagriha, was a monastery gifted to the Buddha by King Bimbisara; also Rigpa Wiki and Wikidata entries.

claim: The following are transliterated Sanskrit names
Kenir transliterates Sanskrit kinnari/kinnara, a term for bone marrow/bone substance
evidence: No source found; kinnara means a celestial being, not bone, so the Sanskrit identification looks doubtful, but not confirmed.

claim: The Sanskrit verse is the Dependent Origination verse (ye dharma hetu)
evidence: Pratityasamutpada gatha: ye dharma hetuprabhava hetum tesam tathagato hyavadat.

claim: Pratimoksha = Individual Liberation; arhat = Conquered the Foe
evidence: Not searched; standard glosses but no source fetched.

claim: Sanskrit title 'Mahashitavani Sutra'
evidence: Note is truncated; colophon preceding is for Mahapratisara, title appears to belong to a different text (Mahasitavati); not verified.

claim: Je Rinpoche = Tsongkhapa, the 14th-century founder of the Sakya school
evidence: Tsongkhapa (1357-1419) founded the Gelug school, not Sakya.
correction: Founder of the Gelug school (1357-1419, 14th-15th century).

claim: Kaushika is an epithet of Indra, king of gods, interlocutor in sutras
evidence: Kausika is an epithet of Sakra/Indra, addressed thus by the Buddha in the Prajnaparamita sutras (84000 Toh 554).

claim: Madhyamaka of Yogic Practice = Yogacara-Madhyamaka
evidence: rnal 'byor spyod pa'i dbu ma is Yogacara-Madhyamaka, founded by Shantarakshita.
